reason: The cited evidence shows that laser cladding can produce well-bonded, hard, wear-resistant coatings on TC4 (E3, E4, E5), and that RHEA coatings can improve corrosion resistance (E1, E2). However, no cited passage directly supports the claim that optimized parameters prevent brittle intermetallics or that the substrate's lightweight and ductile properties are preserved; E2 explicitly notes the presence of intermetallic compounds in a similar system.
premises: Laser cladding can produce a homogeneous RHEA coating with strong metallurgical bonding on TC4
RHEA coatings increase surface hardness and wear resistance via solid-solution strengthening
Optimized laser cladding minimizes thermal gradients, residual stresses, and brittle intermetallics
